title: Check yourself: Building a plugin and publishing it through your own marketplace

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team pushes fresh commits to a plugin whose manifest still says `"version": "1.0.0"`. What reaches installed users?

options.text: The fresh commits at the next launch, since a push always counts
options.says: Ruled out because if the version is not changed, "users don't receive them".

options.text: The fresh commits once the marketplace entry repeats that number
options.says: Ruled out because "Don't set `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry", and Claude Code "then uses the manifest value without warning".

options.text: The fresh commits, since the commit hash is the version
options.says: Ruled out because the commit hash counts only when neither place sets a version: "When neither is set", the commit SHA of the source.

options.text: The copy they already hold, until the number is raised
options.says: The page says users stay on their cached copy until the string changes.

questions.stem: A catalog entry calls a bundle `reviewer-kit`, while the bundle's own manifest says `review-kit`. What happens when someone installs it under the manifest's name?

options.text: An ambiguity message asks which of the two names was meant
options.says: Ruled out because the entry name is "the key Claude Code writes under `enabledPlugins`", and nothing offers a choice between the two names.

options.text: A success message, with the entry name as the skill prefix
options.says: Ruled out because "the manifest name is the prefix of its skills", and the entry name never replaces it.

options.text: A not-found message naming what was typed
options.says: The page says "When the two names differ and someone installs by the manifest name, Claude Code reports `Plugin "<manifest-name>" not found in marketplace "<marketplace>"`."

options.text: A success message, once the catalog has been added again
options.says: Ruled out because "When the two names differ and someone installs by the manifest name, Claude Code reports" a failure, and re-adding the catalog changes neither name.

questions.stem: A repository's settings turn on a bundle whose catalog entry points at a repository of its own. A contributor trusts the folder and starts a session. What do they see?

options.text: A notice that it is enabled but not installed, until they install it
options.says: The page says "Each contributor sees `Plugin "<name>" is enabled in project settings but isn't installed here` in the `/plugin` Errors tab until they run `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace> --scope project`."

options.text: The bundle loaded, since trust is the only condition that applies
options.says: Ruled out because "Only a relative-path plugin installs from the file alone".

options.text: A prompt that lists the hooks of the bundle before it installs
options.says: Ruled out because "Nothing installs, and nothing prompts, until each contributor runs the install."

options.text: The bundle loaded once the marketplace is added to managed settings
options.says: Ruled out because "A repository's own settings reach only the contributors who trust the folder", which is a different channel from managed settings.
